chapter: Piano craft and the New York school
title: Jelly Roll Morton at the Rhythm Club
summary: Morton preached on the corner and held forth at the Harlem musicians' Rhythm Club, gambling and criticizing musicians.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: And the same thing with Jelly Roll Morton. He was unheard of. I remember as a kid where he used to be on the corner, sat on the corner and preach.
When you say preach, what do you mean?

Oh, he used to (whoo!) give lectures on the pros and cons, the shortcomings of musicians, especially the ethnic group, so-called! And he would rave, the guys would listen to him and pucker up their lips behind his back. I didn't feel to good about that. And this was at the Rhythm Club. The Rhythm Club was a club for musicians in Harlem where they had pool tables and card games, and then they had a blackboard, bulletin board for certain different jobs, engagements for the guys.
Was that where he'd hang out?

Oh yes, Jelly Roll would hang out there. And Jelly Roll became a name. You know, 'Oh, Jelly Roll is crazy' -- you know how people are. Because he would always talk, and he'd spend a lot of time on the card games.
Don't you think that perhaps Jelly Roll Morton, being older than most of them, he'd had like his heyday in the Twenties...
Now the guys who came to New York regarded him as old-fashioned.
More or less. I mean, there was a period of inactivity in his life when he didn't really care whether he played a job or not, or something like that.
